argument: At the point the inequality reduces to 2<2, which is false. Equality would be accepted for ≤ but not for <.
Origin substitution accepts x≤3 and rejects x≥3; y≤3 has a different boundary and therefore does not answer the stated question.
Candidate constraint triples are (true,true,true), (true,true,false), (false,true,true). The conjunction accepts only the first.
For each fixed x, all y from 2x+1 upward are required. The strict option omits the boundary and the reversed option takes the opposite side.
Evaluate residual x-y-2 at origin to get -2, selecting its nonpositive side. The third option has a different boundary, even though it also contains the origin.
Multiplying x-y≥-3 by -2 recovers the original exactly. At origin original and first are true, second false; point (0,4) rejects the third equivalence.
The first lies on an included edge. The second has all inequalities strict and is interior. The third lies on an extended boundary line but outside the triangle.
For triangle with vertices (0,0),(4,0),(0,4), the two coordinate half-planes form an unbounded quadrant; (5,5) supplies a concrete false positive removed by the third constraint.
Split into f(R)>0 and f(R)<0; division by its sign gives the appropriate inequality for f(P). The sum criterion fails e.g. f(R)=2,f(P)=-1.
At a boundary reference f(R)=0, both f(R)≤0 and f(R)≥0 are true. The product test then becomes 0≥0 for every P and cannot distinguish any side.
Displacement vectors (1,1) and (2,2) are proportional, with determinant 1*2-1*2=0. This independently confirms zero area and collinearity.
Multiplication of both evaluations by -1 leaves their product unchanged, including zero at the boundary. This orientation invariance requires transforming the reference evaluation too.
